description: High income, high FICO, low DTI, small loan relative to income - should clearly pass.
Comfortably affordable loan over a longer term - the model has no term input, so a longer term must not change the default-risk estimate by itself.
Decent but unremarkable applicant; default probability lands just under the 15% limit.
Good profile but the requested amount is too large to pass; a smaller amount at the same term should be offered as a condition.
Just over the default-probability limit (15.7% vs 15%) with no smaller amount/term found that fits - should refer, not conditions.
Large loan relative to income, high existing debt, weak credit score, and a thin credit file - clearly above the risk limit.
No credit history, low income relative to the loan, weak FICO - should refer.
Loan amount and income given, but no term - the agent must ask, never guess or assume a term.
Loan amount above ~$40,000: outside the personal-loan range the model was trained on. The verdict still runs, but out_of_range must be flagged.

Facts shaped the way a pay stub/bank statement reading would produce them (monthly_income, monthly_debt_payments) rather than annual figures - exercises merge()'s monthly-to-annual and DTI-derivation logic, not just evaluate().
policy_query: what documents confirm income from a bank statement
